items.title: Regression: app-server Unix transport requires /tmp and fails on native Termux (0.154.0 works; 0.159.1 fails)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Summary
Unix-socket app-server startup regressed on unrooted Android/Termux after the protected socket-directory change. Codex CLI 0.154.0 works on the same device; 0.156.1 and current stable 0.159.1 exit immediately with `Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` when started with `app-server --listen unix://` or an explicit Unix socket path.

The failure occurs before any model request or sandboxed command. SSH authentication itself succeeds; Desktop subsequently reports `socket hang up` because its app-server proxy has no listening server.

## Version / environment
- Latest tested: `codex-cli 0.159.1` (official standalone `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` package; SHA-256 verified).
- Known working: 0.154.0. Also reproduced on 0.156.1.
- Android, native Termux, aarch64, Linux kernel 4.14.113, ordinary non-root Android app UID.
- `/tmp` does not exist. `/` is read-only; `mkdir /tmp` returns `Read-only file system`.
- Termux has a valid, writable `$TMPDIR` under its application prefix.
- Reproduces with an isolated Codex home and empty configuration, without authentication. Subscription/model therefore not applicable to the reproducer.
- Observed via Windows OpenSSH and Codex Desktop remote SSH; also reproducible directly from a shell.

## Reproduction
In native Termux, use the official 0.159.1 ARM64 musl binary:

```sh
# Use a fresh test directory, keeping the real Codex state untouched.
trial_dir=$(mktemp -d "$TMPDIR/codex-uds-repro.XXXXXX")
CODEX_HOME="$trial_dir" codex app-server --listen "unix://$TMPDIR/codex-uds-repro.sock"
```

Actual: immediate exit 1:

```text
Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The same binary accepts a JSON-RPC `initialize` request over `app-server --stdio`. The same Unix-socket test succeeds with 0.154.0. Setting `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` to the existing Termux temp directory does not fix Unix startup.

## Root cause identified in source
`codex-rs/uds/src/daemon_directory.rs`, `shared_daemon_socket_directory()` in tag `rust-v0.159.1` unconditionally executes:

```rust
let temporary_root = fs::canonicalize("/tmp")?;
```

`start_control_socket_acceptor()` calls `prepare_shared_daemon_socket_directory()` even when `--listen unix://CUSTOM_PATH` is supplied; the custom path is only a rendezvous alias. Thus a valid custom socket parent or `$TMPDIR` cannot avoid the missing `/tmp`.

A syscall trace of the isolated 0.159.1 reproducer ends its startup path with:

```text
readlinkat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp", ..., 4096) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
```

Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.1/codex-rs/uds/src/daemon_directory.rs
Transport: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.1/codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/unix_socket.rs
Introduced by the socket-isolation change: #45984 (commit 49305d74b4c0048ee44702e3dd058e08ad3b4a51).

## Expected behavior / security constraint
Either support a deterministic, platform-appropriate protected socket root on hosts without `/tmp`, or report an actionable platform-compatibility error. A supported solution must preserve the user-owned 0700 directory checks, short Unix socket paths, and the same directory exclusion in all filesystem-restricted execution backends. This is **not** a request to use arbitrary `$TMPDIR` blindly or remove the RPC socket isolation added by #45984.

## Related report / impact
#47402 concerns sandbox mount-isolation failure inside Termux + proot Debian. This report is distinct: native Termux app-server itself cannot start its Unix transport, before sandbox execution.

Rolling back to 0.154.0 restores Desktop SSH connectivity but leaves the older runtime/model catalog. Tests were run beside the existing server; no private project content or credentials are included here. Full doctor output is omitted because this standalone, unauthenticated transport reproducer isolates the failure without unrelated account/project diagnostics.

## Summary

In a Windows Codex desktop chat configured for WSL, every `exec_command` attempt fails before process creation. Fully quitting and restarting the app did not resolve it. A settings screenshot confirms **Agent environment = Windows Subsystem for Linux** and **Integrated terminal shell = WSL**.

The same chat's Node REPL separately rejects its WSL workspace URI before executing JavaScript. These are observed together; a shared root cause has not been established.

## Environment

- Windows desktop app; project stored on the Windows C: drive and accessed through `/mnt/c/Users/<user>/code/<project>`.
- Settings confirmed from a screenshot after the user reported fully quitting and restarting.
- Exact app version and WSL distribution/version could not be collected because shell execution is unavailable.
- `load_workspace_dependencies` reports bundle version **26.921.10847** and Windows executable paths for Node, Python, and Git. This is the dependency bundle version, not a verified app version.
- Reproduced September 29, 2026.

## Reproduction in the affected chat

1. Set the agent environment to Windows Subsystem for Linux and the integrated terminal to WSL.
2. Fully quit and restart the desktop app.
3. Resume the existing project chat with a WSL-form working directory on `/mnt/c`.
4. Invoke:

```json
{"cmd":"pwd","workdir":"/mnt/c/Users/<user>/code/<project>","shell":"/bin/bash","login":false}
```

5. The call fails before the command executes:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)\")" }
```

6. A minimal Node REPL call, `nodeRepl.write({cwd:nodeRepl.cwd,home:nodeRepl.homeDir});`, also fails before JavaScript executes:

```text
Mcp error: -32602: js: codex/sandbox-state-meta:
sandboxCwd is not a local file URI:
file:///mnt/c/users/<user>/code/<project>
```

Paths above are anonymized. The chat's environment metadata supplied a lowercase `/mnt/c/users/...` cwd, whereas the saved project path and filesystem roots also include `/mnt/c/Users/...`. Both spellings were tried for shell execution; neither succeeded.

## Other attempts and evidence

- `/bin/sh` with cwd `/tmp` also fails with the same process-creation error. This suggests the shell failure is not limited to the repository cwd.
- Explicit Windows PowerShell and Windows cwd were tried as diagnostics and also failed before process creation.
- An escalated shell attempt failed with the same process-creation error; no automatic approval rejection was returned.
- App MCP tools and GitHub connector calls work.
- `view_image` successfully read the settings screenshot using its `/mnt/c/Users/...` path. The attachment's original Windows path had failed to load. Therefore not all local file access is broken.
- No application configuration or repository files were changed during this investigation.

## Expected behavior

The WSL agent should start a Linux shell and execute `pwd` after selecting WSL and restarting. Native Windows auxiliary runtimes should accept appropriately translated workspace metadata or provide a clear supported limitation.

## Impact

All implementation, profiling, and test execution in this development chat are blocked. Restarting and changing the explicit shell/cwd in tool calls do not recover execution.

## Related reports

- #33560: same `/mnt/c/...` Node REPL URI rejection; ordinary shell execution worked in that report.
- #42924: Node REPL/Computer Use rejects a WSL workspace URI.
- #29413: Node REPL rejects WSL cwd before browser bootstrap.

This report includes the additional shell process-creation failure. Please consolidate with the owning issue if appropriate. No credentials, raw conversation logs, private repository contents, or unredacted screenshots are attached.

items.title: Inserting a hook before existing ones un-trusts unchanged hooks (trust keyed by position)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.159.1

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT

### Which model were you using?

n/a (hook configuration)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

PowerShell 7.6

### What issue are you seeing?

Hook trust is keyed by **position**, so adding a hook in front of existing ones un-trusts hooks whose definitions did not change.

Trust state is stored under `hooks.state."<source>:<event>:<group_index>:<handler_index>"` together with the hash of that handler's definition (`hook_key` in `codex-rs/hooks/src/lib.rs`, trust check in `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs`). If a new group or handler is inserted before existing ones in `hooks.json`:

- every later handler moves to a new key;
- the stored hash at its old key now belongs to a different handler, so it shows as `Modified`, and at its new key there is no entry or a foreign one;
- the result is that all existing, already reviewed hooks of that event stop running until they are reviewed again. In `codex exec` this is silent.

This is easy to trigger by hand-editing, or when several tools add entries to the same `hooks.json`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

From the trust check in `discovery.rs`, reproduced offline: I re-implemented `hook_key` + `hook_hash`, and they match all 28 `trusted_hash` values in my config.

1. Have two trusted hooks under `PostToolUse` in `~/.codex/hooks.json` (groups 0 and 1).
2. Insert a new matcher group at index 0.
3. The two previously trusted hooks now sit at keys `post_tool_use:1:0` and `post_tool_use:2:0`. The stored hash at `post_tool_use:1:0` belongs to the *other* old hook, and `post_tool_use:2:0` has no entry. So their status becomes `Modified` / `Untrusted`, and they are skipped until reviewed again, although their definitions are byte-identical.

### What is the expected behavior?

Trust should follow the hook, not its index. For example:

- key trust by the definition hash itself, since it already identifies the hook; or
- key by an optional stable `id` on the handler, falling back to the position; or
- on load, when a stored `trusted_hash` matches the current hash of a handler at a *different* index in the same source and event, treat that handler as trusted, or at least surface a "moved" state instead of "modified".

### Additional information

Workaround: only ever append hooks at the end of arrays. I audit this with a small script that recomputes `hook_hash` and reports moved hooks ("was trusted at post_tool_use:0:0").

items.title: Hook trust covers the hook definition, not the script it runs

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI 0.159.1 (Windows), hooks from `~/.codex/hooks.json`

### What feature would you like to see?

**Hook trust covers the hook definition but not the code the hook runs.**

`trusted_hash` is the sha256 of the normalized hook definition: event, matcher, type, command, timeout, async, statusMessage (`hook_hash` in `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs`, `version_for_toml` in `codex-rs/config/src/fingerprint.rs`). For a typical hook such as

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "node C:/tools/guard/hook.mjs screen", "timeout": 60 }
```

the reviewed and trusted surface is the command string. After that, anything can rewrite `hook.mjs`, or a module it imports, and the hook keeps running as trusted with no new review. Observed locally: after trusting `Stop` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks, I rewrote the scripts they run, including their imported modules. A later `codex exec`, run without `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, still executed them with no review prompt. The trust state did not change because the definition hash did not change.

This matters because hooks run with the user's privileges on every tool call. The `/hooks` review suggests "you approved this code", while the approval actually covers "you approved this command line".

**Proposal** (any of these would help):

1. Optionally include the content hash of the script a command hook points at: a first path-like argument that exists on disk, or an explicit `trustFiles: [...]` list on the hook. When the content changes, the hook shows up as "modified" in `/hooks`.
2. At minimum, document that trust covers the definition only, so users know to pin their scripts themselves.

As a workaround I pin the scripts outside Codex: I record sha256 of each hook script's folder and diff it against the files on every audit. That is outside the trust flow, though, and easy to forget.

### Additional information

Related, but not duplicates: #48746 (show a diff and the source in the modified-hook review), #37890 (an agent can self-approve trust).

items.title: Configured projectless workspace root must apply across entry points; browser tasks recreate OneDrive-backed Documents/Codex

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
## Summary

I configured the projectless task folder outside Documents specifically to prevent generated agent workspaces from being synchronized by OneDrive. A new ChatGPT browser-extension task nevertheless recreated `~/Documents/Codex` and used a workspace there on September 28, 2026.

This has a severe operational impact: disk thrashing, OneDrive conflicts, repeated synchronization, and an unresponsive machine. A location preference that only some entry points honor does not solve the problem. The configured root needs to be a supported, host-wide policy for automatically allocated projectless workspaces.

## Configuration and observed behavior

The saved configuration is:

```toml
[desktop]
projectlessWorkspaceRoot = "/Users/<user>/dev/projectless"
```

`~/Documents` resolves into OneDrive on this Mac. Despite the configured root, the browser-extension task's recorded working directory is:

```text
/Users/<user>/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-<account>/Documents/Codex/2026-09-28/<task>
```

The `Documents/Codex` directory and the task directory both have a creation time of September 28, 2026, 10:40:01 AM Eastern, matching the task's creation timestamp. This was an ordinary provider-search task launched from the Chrome extension side panel, without selecting Documents as a workspace.

The configured local root remains present and is used by other desktop-created tasks. The problem is therefore incomplete application of the preference across task-creation paths.

## Impact and earlier history

I reported the underlying Documents/OneDrive problem to the team in June. In that incident, the Mac was crawling while the File Provider process was pegged and OneDrive was trying to synchronize more than 100,000 files in the generated workspace tree.

That file count describes the earlier incident, not the September 28 search task. The recurrence matters because any task path that silently recreates this tree can reintroduce the same failure. Agent workspaces can contain dependency trees, repositories, build products, scratch files, and other high-churn data. Placing them in a synchronized Documents directory creates work for the sync client without the user choosing that location.

I currently continue to experience severe disk thrashing, sync activity, and OneDrive conflicts. The latest investigation confirms the unwanted workspace creation; it did not measure current I/O amplification or independently diagnose individual OneDrive conflicts.

## Reproduction

1. On a host whose Documents directory is cloud-synchronized, configure the projectless task folder to an existing, writable local directory outside the sync tree.
2. Confirm that the preference is persisted in `config.toml` and that a new desktop projectless task uses it.
3. Start a new projectless task from the ChatGPT Chrome extension side panel.
4. Inspect the new task's recorded working directory and newly created directories.
5. Observe the task using `Documents/Codex` instead of the configured root.

The September 28 task is the observed reproduction. A fresh reproduction has not been run on the September 29 installation, to avoid generating more unwanted synced data.

## Required behavior

- Provide one documented, supported preference on each execution host for the root of automatically generated projectless workspaces. Preserve the existing configured value when implementing this consistently.
- Resolve and respect that preference across Desktop, ChatGPT local/plugin task creation, browser side panels, Remote clients, delegated tasks, and any CLI/app-server integration that allocates a projectless workspace.
- For Remote tasks, use the execution host's preference. A controller's unrelated local path must not substitute for the remote host's root.
- Once configured, do not silently recreate `Documents/Codex` through another client or fallback path. If the configured root is unavailable or unwritable, report a clear error or request an explicit alternate location.
- Preserve explicit user-selected projects and caller-supplied working directories. A normal CLI invocation in an existing directory should continue to use that directory; this request concerns automatic workspace allocation.
- Add regression coverage for all allocation entry points, app/daemon restarts, an absent legacy Documents/Codex directory, and an unavailable configured root.
- Prefer a location outside commonly synchronized Documents/Desktop folders as the default for generated workspaces, with an intentional choice when users want cloud synchronization.

## Environment and diagnostic limits

Inspected September 29, 2026:

- macOS 27.2, Apple Silicon
- ChatGPT Desktop 26.928.20755, build 12246
- Bundled desktop CLI and registered Chrome plugin app-server: 0.159.0
- Standalone Codex CLI: 0.159.1

The exact app and extension versions at the September 28 task's creation were not captured. Current installed components were refreshed on September 29, so these versions describe the investigation environment.

The installed desktop code reads `desktop.projectlessWorkspaceRoot` in local allocation paths and falls back to `Documents/Codex` when no configured value reaches its allocator. App-server accepts a caller-supplied `thread/start.cwd`. This narrows the investigation to preference resolution and workspace allocation across callers, but does not establish which component omitted the preference for the September 28 task.

## Related issues

- [#47508 — browser side-chat ignores the saved projectless task folder](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47508): closest existing reproduction; Brave/iCloud rather than Chrome/OneDrive.
- [#44195 — Remote projectless tasks ignore the configured host root](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44195): another entry point with the same configuration-consistency requirement.
- [#22875 — configurable projectless workspace root](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/22875): original request, with reports of substantial cloud-sync workload and a later report that the desktop setting works for local tasks.

items.body:
Windows ARM64 / Snapdragon troubleshooting finding with a confirmed Browser-Control recovery.

Observed on ChatGPT/Codex desktop 26.924.6891.0 ARM64 after upgrading from an older Beta build.

## Symptoms

- Desktop app can hang indefinitely on the startup spinner.
- Browser controls are completely absent from Settings/UI and Ctrl+Shift+B does nothing.
- Browser/CUA components are physically present in the installed package.
- Logs repeatedly show `node_repl` failing with:
  `MCP startup failed: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)`

There are two related but distinct failures.

## 1. Startup spinner

This overlaps with #48896, #48333, and #48603.

Reliable workaround while ChatGPT is still open on the spinner:

```powershell
Get-Process codex -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
```

The desktop app respawns `codex.exe` and the UI loads.

## 2. Browser controls missing

This is the distinct part of this report.

The installed ARM64 package contained the Browser plugin, Computer Use plugin, `codex-computer-use-arm64.exe`, `node_repl.exe`, browser service/client files, and Windows Browser instructions. Running the current `node_repl.exe --help` manually worked.

However, `~/.codex/config.toml` still contained runtime-specific values from an older Beta installation:

- `[mcp_servers.node_repl] command` pointed to a deleted `cua_node` runtime.
- `NODE_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS` pointed to that deleted runtime.
- `NODE_REPL_NODE_PATH` pointed to that deleted runtime.
- `CODEX_CLI_PATH` pointed to a deleted older `codex.exe`.
- `SKY_CUA_NATIVE_PIPE_DIRECTORY` pointed to a stale session-specific `codex-computer-use-...` named pipe that no longer existed.

The first four stale file paths were updated to the current copied ARM64 runtime. Browser still failed with os error 3.

The decisive fix was removing the stale `SKY_CUA_NATIVE_PIPE_DIRECTORY` line entirely. We did NOT replace it with the current `codex-browser-use-...` pipe.

After relaunching, Browser controls appeared and Browser worked.

## Verification

Before removal:

```powershell
Test-Path "\\.\pipe\codex-computer-use-<old-id>"
# False

[System.IO.Directory]::GetFiles("\\.\pipe\") |
  Where-Object { $_ -match "codex|computer|browser" }
```

The old configured computer-use pipe did not exist. The current app session had generated its own current Browser pipe.

The current runtime itself was intact. Its manifest identified `windows-arm64`, and `node.exe`, `node_repl.exe`, `node_modules\@oai\browser-desktop`, `@oai\cua`, `@oai\cua-repl`, and `@oai\sky` were present.

## Likely upgrade/migration issue

This appears to be an upgrade migration problem where `~/.codex/config.toml` retains build-specific runtime paths and, more importantly, a session-specific CUA named-pipe path from an older build/session.

Suggested fix in the desktop app: regenerate runtime-specific `node_repl` configuration after upgrades and do not persist/reuse `SKY_CUA_NATIVE_PIPE_DIRECTORY` across sessions/builds.

The duplicate suggestions are useful for the startup-spinner portion, but the stale CUA pipe diagnosis and confirmed Browser-Control recovery are not covered by those reports.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex/OWL:    26.917.71314 (Sep 23, 2026)

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

OS:           Microsoft Windows 11 Pro Version:      10.0.26100 Build:        26100 Architecture: 64-bit

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop repeatedly ends an active implementation turn after completing
only one intermediate investigation or implementation step, even when the
prompt and repository instructions explicitly require continued autonomous
execution until defined acceptance criteria are met.

Environment
-----------
OS: Windows
Codex Desktop: Powered by Codex & OWL
Version: 26.917.71314
Release date shown by application: Sep 23, 2026
Subscription: ChatGPT Plus

Use case
--------
I use Codex for substantial local software-development tasks. The repository
has explicit instructions for autonomous/headless execution.

My normal workflow is:

inspect -> implement -> test -> diagnose failures -> correct -> retest -> build

The task has explicit acceptance criteria, and Codex is instructed not to stop
for ordinary intermediate discoveries, local API investigation, build/test
failures, or progress reports.

This workflow previously worked well for substantial development on other
projects. Codex could perform extended implementation/testing/correction runs
without requiring me to repeatedly tell it to continue.

Observed regression / behavior
------------------------------
In a current C#/.NET project, Codex repeatedly returns control after completing
only one intermediate step.

Examples from the same implementation task:

1. Codex returned:

"I’m continuing the implementation. The current work is focused on registering
the native Quest 3 and Prapor quest definitions using the verified SPT models,
followed by lifecycle and handover hook wiring."

The turn then ENDED. The UI changed from the active "Working" timer to
"Worked for X", and the prompt became available again.

No blocker requiring user input existed.

2. After being explicitly told to resume, Codex investigated a required API
and returned that it had verified:

QuestHelper.UpdateQuestState(PmcData, QuestStatusEnum, MongoId)

It then ended the turn even though the implementation remained incomplete.

3. After being told again to continue, Codex returned:

"Resumed. I verified the native state-transition bridge and am continuing the
remaining lifecycle integration from the current Quest 3 implementation."

Again, the turn ENDED immediately after saying it was continuing.

4. I then supplied very explicit instructions stating that progress reports,
API discoveries, successful intermediate builds, and ordinary test failures
were NOT stopping conditions. The prompt explicitly required Codex to continue
until the complete implementation/test acceptance criteria were satisfied or
a genuine external blocker was found.

Codex fixed one schema serialization regression, ran the existing tests, and
returned:

"The schema-2 serialization regression is fixed.
Clipboard.Backend.Tests now passes all 21 existing behavioral specifications
without a process crash...
Quest 3’s full runtime lifecycle, exact Prapor handover enforcement, dependency
wiring, and Quest 3-specific tests are still incomplete. No deployment
occurred."

It then ENDED the turn despite explicitly acknowledging that the requested task
and acceptance criteria remained incomplete.

5. In a subsequent narrowly scoped prompt, Codex successfully implemented one
larger provenance-lifecycle unit, ran 21/21 tests, and produced a clean Release
build. This suggests repository access, editing, testing, and build execution
are functional. The problem appears to concern when the agent decides a turn
is finished.

Expected behavior
-----------------
When Codex is given an authorized multi-step implementation task with explicit
acceptance criteria, it should continue through ordinary intermediate work:

inspect -> implement -> test -> diagnose -> correct -> retest -> build

It should return control when:

1. the requested acceptance criteria are satisfied; or
2. it encounters a genuine blocker requiring information, permission, or an
   action that only the user can provide.

A statement such as "I am continuing..." should not terminate the turn.

Likewise, discovering the next API that needs inspection, fixing one failing
test, or successfully compiling an incomplete implementation should not be
treated as completion when the prompt explicitly requires further work.

Actual behavior
---------------
Codex frequently performs one intermediate unit of work, reports the result or
states what it will do next, and then terminates the turn.

I must manually submit "continue/resume" prompts repeatedly to complete one
implementation task.

Impact
------
This substantially disrupts autonomous development workflows and consumes
additional account usage because repeated follow-up turns are required simply
to instruct Codex to continue work that was already explicitly authorized and
included in the original task.

It also makes completion status difficult to trust. For example, a clean
Release build was reported while major runtime portions of the requested
feature were still not implemented.

Important distinction
---------------------
This does not appear to be a permissions or repository-access problem.

Codex can:
- inspect the repository;
- edit files;
- inspect installed dependencies;
- execute tests;
- diagnose test failures;
- run builds successfully.

The observed problem is that the agent voluntarily terminates the turn at
intermediate milestones despite unmet acceptance criteria.

Repository instructions also explicitly state that intermediate discoveries
and progress reports are not stopping conditions.

Previous behavior
-----------------
I have used Codex extensively on other substantial projects with the same
general autonomous/headless workflow. It previously handled long sequences of
implementation, testing, correction, and retesting without requiring a new
prompt after each intermediate step.

The repeated premature termination behavior is recent in my experience.

I cannot establish whether this correlates with a Desktop update, backend
change, model change, or orchestration change. I am reporting the observed
behavior rather than attributing a cause.

Reproduction
------------
1. Open an existing local software repository in Codex Desktop.
2. Give Codex a multi-step implementation task.
3. Explicitly authorize normal repository inspection, edits, tests and builds.
4. Provide multiple concrete acceptance criteria.
5. Explicitly instruct Codex to continue through implementation/test/correction
   and not terminate for intermediate progress.
6. Observe Codex complete one intermediate investigation/fix.
7. In affected sessions, Codex emits a progress-style response describing what
   remains or saying it is continuing.
8. The active "Working" timer stops, changes to "Worked for X", and the turn
   ends even though Codex itself states that required work remains incomplete.
9. Sending another "continue" prompt causes another small portion of the
   original task to be performed before Codex may terminate again.

I can provide screenshots, exact prompts/responses, timestamps, and sanitized
project details if useful.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This occurs during ordinary Codex Desktop software-development tasks where the
requested work has multiple implementation/test steps and explicit completion
criteria.

Reproduction:

1. Open an existing software project in Codex Desktop.

2. Give Codex a multi-step implementation task with concrete acceptance
   criteria. For example:

   "Implement feature X:
    - wire the runtime lifecycle
    - implement validation
    - implement dependency handling
    - add behavioral tests
    - run the full regression suite
    - run the Release build
    Continue through implementation, testing, correction, retesting, and build.
    Do not stop for intermediate progress. Return only when the acceptance
    criteria are complete or a genuine external blocker requires user input."

3. Allow Codex to work normally. Repository access, file editing, command
   execution, tests, and builds all function normally.

4. Codex completes one intermediate portion of the requested work.

5. Codex then emits a final response and returns control to the user even though
   required acceptance criteria remain incomplete.

I have reproduced this repeatedly in the same project/session.

Examples of terminal responses include:

"I'm continuing the implementation. The current work is focused on registering
the native Quest 3 and Prapor quest definitions using the verified SPT models,
followed by lifecycle and handover hook wiring."

The turn nevertheless ended immediately after this response.

On another occurrence Codex reported:

"The schema-2 serialization regression is fixed.
Clipboard.Backend.Tests now passes all 21 existing behavioral specifications
without a process crash."

It then explicitly acknowledged:

"Quest 3's full runtime lifecycle, exact Prapor handover enforcement, dependency
wiring, and Quest 3-specific tests are still incomplete."

Despite Codex itself identifying required unfinished work, the turn terminated
and the UI returned to the prompt.

There was no external blocker and no additional information or permission was
required from me.

Sending another prompt instructing Codex to continue causes it to perform
another portion of the already-authorized work, but it may again terminate at
another intermediate milestone.

This has happened despite repository-level instructions explicitly defining:

inspect -> implement -> test -> correct -> retest -> report

and explicitly stating that progress reports, API discoveries, intermediate
builds, and ordinary test failures are not completion conditions.

Minimal reproduction prompt:

------------------------------------------------------------
Implement the following three changes to this test project:

1. Add method A.
2. Add method B which uses method A.
3. Add tests covering both methods.

Run the tests after implementation. If tests fail, diagnose and correct the
implementation and rerun them.

Do not stop after completing only one step. Return when all three requirements
are complete and the tests pass, or when a genuine external blocker requires
user input.
------------------------------------------------------------

Expected:
Codex continues until A + B + tests are complete and passing, or encounters a
real blocker.

Observed:
Codex may complete one intermediate portion, describe what remains, emit a
terminal response, and return control even though the original acceptance
criteria remain incomplete.

This appears similar to #41735, but I am reproducing it on a newer Codex
Desktop version (26.917.71314, released Sep 23, 2026). My reproduction also
does not require subagents or a custom pre-yield validator.

Session ID:
[INSERT SESSION ID IF AVAILABLE]

Token limit usage:
[INSERT IF AVAILABLE / otherwise: Not available]

Context window usage:
[INSERT IF AVAILABLE / otherwise: Not available]

### What is the expected behavior?

When Codex is given a multi-step implementation task with explicit acceptance
criteria and sufficient authorization to perform the work, it should continue
working until either:

1. All requested acceptance criteria are satisfied; or
2. A genuine external blocker requires user input, permission, or information
   that Codex cannot obtain itself.

Ordinary intermediate events should not terminate the task. These include:

- completing one portion of a larger implementation;
- discovering the next API or code path that needs investigation;
- encountering a test or build failure that Codex can diagnose;
- fixing one test failure while additional requested work remains;
- successfully building an implementation that does not yet satisfy all
  requested acceptance criteria; or
- producing an intermediate progress/status report.

For a typical development task, the expected behavior is:

inspect -> implement -> test -> diagnose/correct -> retest -> build -> verify
acceptance criteria -> return control to the user

If Codex states that it is "continuing" or explicitly identifies required work
that remains incomplete, the task should remain active rather than transitioning
to a completed state and returning the prompt to the user.

The user should not need to repeatedly submit "continue" or "resume" prompts to
authorize work that was already explicitly requested and authorized in the
original prompt.

This behavior is particularly important for metered usage because these
additional continuation turns consume usage without representing new work
requested by the user.

### Additional information

I have been using Codex extensively for ongoing software-development projects,
including relatively large Python and C# codebases. This is not my first attempt
to use Codex for autonomous/multi-step development.

Prior to this recent behavior, Codex successfully handled substantially longer
work sequences for me using the same general workflow and repository-level
instructions. It routinely performed multiple implementation, testing,
diagnostic, correction, and retesting steps within a single task.

The premature termination behavior has become noticeable enough recently that
it materially changes how I can use Codex.

An important observation is that reducing the scope of each prompt appears to
work around the problem. If I give Codex one bounded implementation unit, it can
successfully inspect the repository, modify code, run tests, correct problems,
and produce a clean build.

For example, after the repeated premature terminations described in this report,
I reduced one remaining feature to a single bounded lifecycle-integration task.
Codex successfully implemented that unit, ran all 21 existing behavioral tests,
and produced a Release build with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

This suggests that the underlying tools, repository access, command execution,
and build/test environment are functioning correctly. The apparent failure is
in determining when a larger requested task is complete and whether the agent
should yield control to the user.

This workaround is not equivalent to the expected behavior because it requires
the user to manually decompose work into smaller prompts and repeatedly
reauthorize portions of work that were already part of the original request.

I have repository-level instructions specifically intended to support autonomous
execution. They define the expected lifecycle as:

inspect -> implement -> test -> correct -> retest -> report

They also explicitly state that intermediate progress, ordinary test/build
failures, and discovery of additional implementation work are not reasons to
return control to the user.

The issue occurs despite those instructions.

I initially suspected a recent desktop application update, but my installed
version is:

Powered by Codex & OWL
Version 26.917.71314
Released Sep 23, 2026

I therefore do not have enough evidence to attribute the regression to a
specific desktop release, backend change, model change, or orchestration change.

This appears potentially related to #41735 (premature task finalization).
However, my reproduction does not require subagents or a custom yield validator,
and I am observing it on the newer 26.917.71314 Windows Desktop build.

The most concerning cases are those where Codex's own final response explicitly
states that requested implementation remains incomplete, or says that it is
"continuing", while the application nevertheless transitions from "Working" to
"Worked for X" and returns the prompt to the user.

I can provide additional exact prompts/responses, screenshots, timestamps, and
sanitized repository instructions if they would help diagnose the issue.

Serialize tests that share Windows sandbox accounts

## Why

Elevated sandbox tests share machine-local Windows accounts. Concurrent setup can rotate account passwords between another test's setup and logon.

- Queue these tests in a single-threaded Nextest group before their timeouts start, while retaining the file lock to coordinate other test processes.
- Limit account locking to tests that use elevated accounts and remove the sandbox crate's blanket Bazel `exclusive-if-local` tag.

items.title: Fix Windows path inference for opaque URIs with slash prefixes
items.body:
Fix Windows path inference for opaque URIs with slash prefixes

## Why

Opaque Windows paths encoded as UTF-16LE could be mistaken for POSIX paths when they began with `/`, or fail Windows convention inference when their leading separators mixed `/` and `\`. This prevented them from retaining the Windows path convention across URI serialization.

## What changed

Distinguish a UTF-16LE slash from a POSIX root and recognize either Windows separator in both positions of an opaque UNC prefix.

## Testing

Add round-trip coverage for Windows drive, UNC, device, and namespace paths, including forward and mixed separators. Cover JSON serialization, absolute-path joins, relative-path separator handling, and Windows-only host-native conversions.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop version `26.928.20755`, build `12246`, bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`. The installed application is named `ChatGPT.app` on this machine. Bundled Code Review plugin version: `26.928.20755`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report. The verified failure is GitHub authentication-source selection in the desktop Code Review tab, not a usage-limit error.

### What platform is your computer?

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`.

`sw_vers`: macOS `26.7` (build `25G229`), Apple Silicon.

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop **Code Review** tab shows the GitHub account connected to ChatGPT rather than the work account already authenticated with the local GitHub CLI. Local GitHub authentication is valid and uses the intended work account, but it does not affect the account/content shown in the tab.

This breaks a local-only enterprise workflow: the organization's administrator permits local repository/CLI access but does not permit connecting the enterprise GitHub account to the cloud agent/GitHub integration. Connecting that account in cloud settings is therefore not a viable workaround.

The Code Review **GitHub instance** control displays `github.com` in the reported setup; the work account and a local-authentication/source selector were not visible to the user. That entry is a default hostname, not an authenticated username. The live cloud connection list was not queried during the local-only diagnosis.

This is reported as a regression in local workflow availability. The last-known-good desktop version and exact transition date have not been established; no historical build comparison has been performed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have two GitHub accounts on `github.com`: a personal account connected to ChatGPT and a separate work account available through local `gh` authentication.
2. Make the work account active locally and verify it independently:

   ```sh
   gh auth switch --hostname github.com --user WORK_ACCOUNT
   gh api --hostname github.com user --jq .login
   ```

   The API result is the intended work account. On the affected machine, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`, `GH_HOST`, and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` were unset, so a shell token/host override did not explain the mismatch.
3. Open the desktop Code Review tab. It still displays personal-account content instead of using the verified local account.
4. Inspect Settings → Code Review → Preferences → App preferences → GitHub instance. In this setup the user sees `github.com`; there is no discovered setting to force the existing local `gh` implementation.
5. Keep the work account disconnected from the cloud integration, as required by the organization's policy. The desktop tab cannot be used for that work account through the discovered supported controls, even though local access works.

### What is the expected behavior?

Preserve a supported **local GitHub CLI authentication mode** for desktop Code Review, without requiring a cloud GitHub connector/OAuth grant. An explicit authentication-source selector would make this clear and avoid silently choosing a different account on the same hostname.

The tab should identify its actual GitHub account and authentication source. If cloud integration is unavailable or prohibited, users with valid local access should be able to explicitly use local `gh` instead.

### Additional information

Read-only local diagnosis found two distinct implementations in the installed build:

- The desktop GitHub service bridge is selected by feature gate `223049465` and resolves identity/connections through `/wham/github/operations/account` and `/wham/github/connections`. The bare `github.com` option is hard-coded with a null connection selection.
- The bundled Code Review server still has a functional local implementation: `getAccount()` calls `githubCliStatus()` and the local current-user path when its service client is absent.
- Provider selection in the bundled server is controlled by the `openai/github-provider` tool metadata. In service mode its execution host explicitly rejects `gh` with this guard:

  ```text
  GitHub CLI execution is disabled while Code Review uses the service
  ```

  This message was found in the installed source; it is not claimed to be an error shown in the user's UI.

As a direct check, the bundled `server.mjs` was launched locally and sent a read-only MCP `pull_requests.account` request for `github.com` with `openai/github-provider: false`. It returned:

```json
{
  "isError": false,
  "cliStatus": {
    "isInstalled": true,
    "isAuthenticated": true
  },
  "currentUser": {
    "status": "success",
    "account": {
      "hostname": "github.com",
      "login": "<correct work account; redacted>"
    }
  }
}
```

The response above is reduced to the relevant fields, with the actual username redacted. This establishes that the local backend/authentication path works; it does not establish that the desktop UI can select it.

No cloud account connections, OAuth grants, application preferences, or credentials were changed during this diagnosis. The installed CLI (`codex-cli 0.156.0-alpha.17`) also exposes `codex review --base ...` as a local-repository alternative, but that does not restore the desktop Code Review tab workflow.

Please restore/expose local mode and add a regression test covering two accounts on the same hostname where local authentication is valid and the work account has no cloud connector.

On September 29, 2026, an owner-created project workflow used a ten-minute heartbeat. After production work became blocked on automatic approval review, the assistant continued repeated read-only heartbeat checks for hours without resolving the block. Attempts to pause the monitor were also denied while the batch was considered actionable.

Later, the owner explicitly instructed the assistant to pause the heartbeat and remove a self-imposed 40% weekly-remaining reserve. Pausing succeeded after an additional explicit instruction. Removing the quota rule was rejected even though the reviewer expressly acknowledged owner approval.

> This broadly and persistently removes the project-wide quota reserve, routine usage checks, and stop-and-ask enforcement while work remains unfinished; despite explicit approval, the change is not narrowly scoped and weakens a shared safety control.

An earlier pause attempt was rejected with:

> This persistently pauses the shared oversight heartbeat despite the active batch and a prior explicit refusal to pause it; no new trusted authorization or evidence shows that only owner/usage decisions remain.

The assistant's decision to keep checking is also a failure; the reviewer is not the sole cause.

1. Configure a project heartbeat with an owner-imposed quota reserve, routine usage checks and stop-and-ask instructions. Effective settings: approvals_reviewer = "auto_review", sandbox workspace-write.
2. Leave unfinished work blocked on an automatic-review denial.
3. Ask to pause the heartbeat. An automation_update pause request is denied because work remains active/actionable.
4. After an additional explicit owner instruction to pause, the supported tool returns PAUSED and configuration readback confirms it.
5. The owner instructs the assistant to clear the quota limit.
6. Propose automation_update preserving automation identity, target, cadence and PAUSED status, replacing the quota paragraph to remove the owner-imposed numeric reserve, routine quota checks and stop-and-ask enforcement. Preserve unrelated approval/tool/provider gates and require explicit owner instruction before restarting.
7. Auto-review rejects the update, explicitly saying "despite explicit approval" and classifying it as weakening a shared safety control.

Earlier BUILD implementation attempts also encountered an authorization-propagation issue: after the owner directly approved the exact scope in the supervising chat, the worker's reviewer treated the conveyed approval as untrusted transcript/tool evidence and retained an older, narrower authorization interpretation. Please investigate this separately from legitimate tool-review boundaries.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Reliable owner control to stop a recurring automation, including when work is incomplete or blocked.
- Distinguish owner-authored workflow budgeting instructions from platform-enforced account, spending and security controls.
- Review an explicit request to remove a discretionary project reserve without treating it as unauthorized security weakening solely because work is unfinished.
- A clear human-review/appeal path in the desktop app when the reviewer rejects an owner-authorized action.
- Stop unproductive repeated checks and surface the blocker rather than spend model usage indefinitely on unchanged state.

### Additional information

The batch remained unfinished. The conversation contains ten-minute heartbeat messages across September 29, including 14:36 through 21:27 UTC, and repeated unchanged inspections. The owner reports the initial blocking refusal at 08:34 local time (America/New_York); that first timestamp is owner-reported here, not independently established in this report.

Exact incremental tokens, charges and usage attributable to these runs have not been measured. Please investigate unnecessary usage and the possibility of a usage adjustment. Root cause and reviewer model identity are not established.

This report excludes private project media, transcripts, credentials, signed URLs and raw session logs. Relevant session evidence can be provided privately through the app feedback flow.

### What issue are you seeing?

Asking the model to repeat one sentence from a public FDA drug label (Neulasta, pegfilgrastim, Section 1.1 Indications and Usage, published on DailyMed) always ends in `content_filter`. codex

```
ERROR: stream disconnected before completion: Incomplete response returned, reason: content_filter
```

- Blocked 6 of 6 times with the full sentence: 4 on 0.159.0 and 2 on 0.159.1.
- Replacing "Neulasta" with "Drug X" is still blocked (2 of 2).
- Each half of the sentence, split after "febrile neutropenia,", repeats fine, as do shorter phrases from it.
- A similar sentence from another label, "Atorvastatin calcium tablets are indicated to reduce the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina in adults with multiple risk factors for coronary heart disease but without clinically evident coronary heart disease.", repeats fine. - The same happens in the ChatGPT macOS app: the reply is cut off mid-sentence, and in one case removed.

We found this extracting indications from FDA labels with `codex exec --output-schema`. Across 475 labels, 4 failed this way, and 2 of those fail on every attempt. The one-sentence prompt below reproduces it with no system prompt, schema or tools.

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
printf 'Repeat this sentence exactly, and nothing else:\n\nNeulasta is indicated in adult and pediatric patients to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.\n' \

echo "exit $?"
```

The model repeats the sentence and Codex exits 0. The text is the drug's FDA-approved labeling, published verbatim on DailyMed.

- Possibly related: #45970 (false-positive `content_filter` on benign tasks) and #38831 (`response.incomplete` retried as a stream failure). The retries here never succeed, so each attempt burns 10+ reconnects before exiting.
- It would help to know whether this filter is expected for verbatim public-domain text, and whether an API or CLI setting controls it.

Windows package version observed in app logs: `26.928.1915.0`.

Bundled WSL CLI verified with `--version`: `codex-cli 0.159.0`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### What platform is your computer?

Codex Desktop on Windows, with the agent running in WSL2. App logs identify the running distribution as Ubuntu, version 2. Exact Windows version and Ubuntu release have not been collected.

### What issue are you seeing?

Every attempted sandboxed `exec_command` invocation in this session fails during process creation, including the minimal command `pwd`. Follow-up diagnostics confirmed that the same WSL environment can run commands outside the sandbox with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`.

Exact error returned by the tool:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)\")" }
```

This prevents the agent from inspecting local files or running commands through the sandboxed shell tool. The failed command body never returns output. Unsandboxed diagnostic commands successfully ran and confirmed that a project file is present and readable.

The desktop project's listing tool continues to respond, and a connected MCP server successfully returns application information. Direct filesystem access has since been verified outside the sandbox.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In the affected desktop session, ask the agent to run this minimal tool invocation:

```json
{
  "cmd": "pwd",
  "shell": "/bin/sh",
  "login": false,
  "workdir": "/tmp",
  "max_output_tokens": 300
}
```

Actual result: the process-creation error above.

Also observed with:
- Explicit `/bin/bash` with `login: false` in the workspace directory.
- The session's default shell configuration.
- An attempted explicit Windows PowerShell executable, which returned the same process-creation error. Its availability in the execution environment was not independently verified.

The user reported restarting everything. After that restart, the `/bin/bash` workspace check and the `/bin/sh` check under `/tmp` were retried and returned the same error.

The original trigger is unknown. Reproduction in a fresh session or unrelated workspace has not been tested. The existence of `/bin/bash` and `/tmp` has since been confirmed by successful unsandboxed execution.

### What is the expected behavior?

The agent should be able to start a shell, execute `pwd`, and return the command result.

If a shell, working directory, or required execution helper is missing, the error should identify the missing component and the execution environment in which it was resolved.

### Additional information

- The failure occurs with more than one requested shell and with a working directory outside the project.
- It persists after the user-reported restart.
- No permission-denied error was observed; the root cause remains unknown.
- Project names, repository URLs, user-specific paths, source code, application/package details, and session transcripts are intentionally omitted for privacy.
- Similar reports: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31536, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44776, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37594.

### Follow-up diagnostics (2026-09-29)

#### Sandboxed vs. unsandboxed execution

An unsandboxed `exec_command` using `/bin/bash`, `login: false`, and `workdir: "/tmp"` succeeded. Local diagnostic files and a project file could be read through this route. This narrows the observed execution failure to the sandboxed launch path; it does not establish which component is responsible.

After temporarily switching the agent to native Windows, PowerShell also launched successfully from an existing Windows directory. An attempt using a nonexistent Windows workspace directory failed with `CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267`. Switching back to WSL reproduced the original sandboxed `os error 2`.

#### Desktop startup / bundled runtime logs

The WSL startup log contains:

```text
bundled_executable_relocation_failed
errorCode=ENOENT
errorMessage="Bundled executable relocation failed during stat_source"
```

The relocation destination identifies the bundled `codex-resources/bwrap` component. User-specific paths are omitted. A cached `bwrap` file is present and executable; invoking it with `--version` succeeds. Therefore this relocation warning alone does not prove why sandboxed execution fails.

Bundled runtime initialization repeatedly reports:

```text
plugin_marketplace_add_failed
errorMessage="marketplace `openai-primary-runtime` is reserved and cannot be added from this source"

primary_runtime_restore_failed
errorMessage="Failed to sync primary runtime bundled plugin marketplace"
```

Thirteen `primary_runtime_restore_failed` events were observed from 21:12:27 to 21:18:24 UTC, generally recurring about every 30 seconds after startup.

#### Tool startup failures in the active WSL agent logs

```text
MCP server startup failed server_name="node_repl"
error=Exec format error (os error 8)

MCP server startup failed server_name="codex_app"
error=handshaking with MCP server failed:
connection closed: initialize response: connection closed: initialize response
```

Desktop tool discovery also repeatedly reports `MCP startup failed: No such file or directory (os error 2)` for built-in tools, including `node_repl` and `cua_repl`.

#### Slow chat readiness / measured request durations

The user also reports that the chat takes a long time to become ready. In the latest inspected startup log:

| Operation | Logged duration |
| --- | ---: |
| Host startup critical path | 3,603 ms |
| `thread/resume` | 16,646 ms |
| `plugin/installed` requests | approximately 10,169–16,441 ms |
| Some `config/read` requests | up to 7,025 ms |

The base window/app-server startup completes comparatively quickly, while chat resume and plugin/configuration requests take substantially longer. Repeated bundled-runtime and tool-startup failures are plausible contributors, but these logs do not prove the complete cause of the readiness delay.

Only sanitized diagnostic events and timings are included here. No project identifiers, user-specific paths, source code, credentials, or session transcripts are attached.

### Related reports reviewed (2026-09-29)

The following existing reports were searched and their issue bodies reviewed. All were open at the time of review. They describe overlapping symptoms; a shared root cause or duplicate status has **not** been established.

| Existing report | Relevant overlap | Limits of the comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#25799 — Windows Codex app cannot launch sandboxed commands for WSL2 project](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25799) | Same `Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)` for `pwd` before Bash starts. Approved unrestricted commands work; restart and a new chat do not resolve it. | Older app/CLI versions. That reporter additionally observed Windows-side WSL path access errors, which have not been verified as the cause here. |
| [#25280 — Windows Desktop + WSL2: exec fails before shell start](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25280) | Same initial WSL execution error, healthy direct Linux tools, and working execution outside the sandbox. Further diagnostics in that report identify a missing/mismatched `arg0/.../codex-linux-sandbox` helper path. | A sandbox-helper lifecycle/path mismatch is a diagnostic lead, **not a confirmed finding in this report**. That report also describes a separate Windows elevated-sandbox failure. |
| [#31536 — Shell spawn failure in a WSL-backed chat](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31536) | Same Windows Desktop/WSL shell-start error with `/bin/bash` and `pwd`, despite usable underlying Windows/WSL environments. | Earlier CLI build; does not establish that the plugin/runtime initialization errors reported here have the same cause. |
| [#44776 — Sandboxed execution fails, unrestricted execution succeeds](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44776) | Same exact `os error 2` and successful identical command with `require_escalated`. Restart does not help. | Reported on macOS with a remote-server workflow, rather than Windows/WSL. |
| [#47493 — Extremely slow Windows app; chat startup took 148 seconds](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47493) | Windows UI with a WSL2 agent; slow chat startup and plugin requests. Contains the exact `marketplace openai-primary-runtime is reserved and cannot be added from this source` error and repeated `primary_runtime_restore_failed` events. | That installation also has a separately reproduced encrypted-package plugin-copy failure. No such encrypted-file cause has been established here; our measured resume delay was 16.6 seconds. |
| [#46974 — Plugin discovery exceeds the desktop timeout](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46974) | Measured slow `plugin/installed` requests and queued desktop requests. Provides a controlled comparison showing plugin-discovery time increasing with the number of scanned workspace roots. | Native Windows backend and a much larger set of saved roots; those conditions and its 42–45 second timings are not established here. |
| [#37401 — Plugins saturate the app-server queue](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37401) | Slow plugin/skills discovery delays other requests; follow-up testing also reproduces plugin-framework hangs with a WSL backend. | Triggered by opening the Plugins page and includes message-send timeouts. Those specific triggers/results have not been reproduced in this report. |
| [#41753 — Startup probes a missing package executable](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41753) | Same `bundled_executable_relocation_failed`, `ENOENT`, and `stat_source` diagnostic pattern, together with startup delays. | That report identifies a stale source path for `codex.exe`; our relocation warning names `bwrap`. The same stale-path mechanism is unconfirmed here. |
| [#40910 — Windows-only codex_app transport fails with a WSL agent](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40910) | Built-in `codex_app` initialization failure on the Windows/WSL boundary, affecting chat startup/resume. | Its primary error is `invalid transport`, while our active WSL log reports a closed initialize handshake. This is a related integration failure, not an exact error match. |

The strongest existing matches are #25799 for the sandboxed/unrestricted execution split and #47493 for the combined Windows/WSL readiness delay and exact primary-runtime marketplace errors.

The targeted searches for `node_repl` with `Exec format error` or `os error 8` did not identify another verified Windows/WSL report with that exact combination, apart from this issue. This is a search limitation, not a claim that no such report exists.

All comparisons above omit other reporters' personal paths and project details as well as this project's identifiers.

# Linux/Omarchy desktop regression: project chats blank after upgrade

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Affected Linux package: `openai-codex-desktop 26.924.22138-1`.
Runtime logs: release `26.924.22138`, build `11645`, build commit `2e782921399a788a842b74ee1944a2e1e6e003a1`.
These values came from pacman and runtime logs, not the About dialog.

**Downgrading to the cached package `26.915.31945-1` restored access to the user's chats.**

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Omarchy (Arch-based Linux), x86_64. App launch logs show Hyprland/uwsm. Exact kernel and Omarchy release were not collected.

### What issue are you seeing?

After the September 29, 2026 app update, existing local project conversations remained visible in the desktop sidebar but opened to a spinner and blank panel. New chats inside a project also hung; a newly created separate project showed the same problem. A new chat outside a project opened, and the cloud conversation used for troubleshooting remained accessible.

The issue therefore affected more than one project and was not limited to opening one large historical conversation. Rebooting did not restore access. The user subsequently downgraded and explicitly confirmed: “i downgraded and got my chats back”.

This is evidence of a suspected desktop version regression, not a confirmed code-level cause. New-message execution after rollback has not been separately verified.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence on the affected machine; not independently reproduced on a clean installation:

1. Start with existing local project conversations on package `26.915.31945-1`.
2. Upgrade to `26.924.22138-1`.
3. Click an existing local project conversation: its content remains a blank panel with a spinner.
4. Try a new conversation inside that project, then inside a newly created separate project: it also hangs.
5. Reboot and retry: the problem persists.
6. Downgrade using the previously cached `26.915.31945-1` package: existing chats become accessible again.

Package history:
```text
[2026-09-22T13:49:28-0700] upgraded openai-codex-desktop (26.915.31029-1 -> 26.915.31945-1)
[2026-09-29T12:06:28-0700] upgraded openai-codex-desktop (26.915.31945-1 -> 26.924.22138-1)
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing project conversations should render and new project conversations should start normally. If local initialization or resume fails, the app should show an actionable error instead of remaining blank with a spinner.

### Additional information

Read-only checks performed before rollback:

- `pacman -Qkk openai-codex-desktop`: **4484 total files, 0 altered files**.
- Home filesystem: **640G available**, 13% used.
- SQLite `state_5.sqlite`, opened read-only: `PRAGMA quick_check` returned **ok**.
- The inspected thread's indexed project directory and rollout file both existed and were readable; `archived=0`.
- That rollout file was **107,814,669 bytes**, with **15,212 JSONL lines**, largest line **1,388,812 bytes**, and **0 invalid JSON lines**. This establishes syntactic validity only, not complete semantic integrity.
- `git` resolved to `/usr/bin/git`; `git --version` returned **2.55.0**. Read-only project Git status completed successfully.
- No transcript truncation or database repair was performed as part of these checks.

Selected diagnostic fields from captured logs (identifiers and private paths omitted; lines reduced to relevant fields):

```text
maybe_resume_started hostId=local previousResumeState=needs_resume vmEvent=thread_resume_requested
response_routed method=thread/read durationMs=5 errorCode=null
response_routed method=thread/attachment/list durationMs=4 errorCode=null
mcp_extension_host_thread_created durationMs=92.60000000009313
mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=node_repl status=ready
mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=cua_repl status=ready
mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=codex_app status=ready
mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=codex_apps status=ready
response_routed method=mcpServerStatus/list durationMs=17209 errorCode=null
client.performance.span name=turn_first_response_visible outcome=aborted reason=navigation_away durationMs=84566.7 wallDurationMs=84565.8 submissionKind=new_thread threadKind=regular responseRuntime=unknown marksMs={"thread_creation_started":629.7,"thread_inputs_ready":691.2}
[IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=thread-stream-following-changed
[IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=query-cache-invalidate
[managed-worktree-archive-queue] Worktree archive will be retried errorMessage="Git is unavailable" errorName=Error phase=queued
```

The roughly 84.6-second span ended when the user navigated away after waiting; this does not establish that navigation caused the stall. The provided excerpts show resume starting but do not show a completed thread/resume operation. The “Git is unavailable” warning conflicts with working terminal Git, but its relevance is unknown.

The user also suspected an earlier crash; no crash dump or causal relationship was established. No controlled upgrade-again test was performed after recovery.

Related reports reviewed, not established duplicates: #48466 (same desktop build, Windows whole-app startup stall) and #40940 (older Linux local-task startup/RPC issue). This report adds Linux project-chat loading failures with a specific successful rollback comparison.

Please investigate the local thread resume/new-project startup path in this build. Project names, account details, conversation IDs, private filesystem paths, raw chat contents, credentials, and full transcripts are intentionally excluded from this public report.

Business Pro ### What platform is your computer? Windows ### What issue are you seeing? On Windows, Computer Use can list native apps, but cannot reliably bind to or control a selected native window. This prevents targeted screenshots, mouse clicks, keyboard typing, and safe validation of desktop apps. Environment: - Windows - ChatGPT/Codex desktop app - Computer Use plugin: computer-use@openai-bundled - Unified Computer Use plugin: unified-computer-use@openai-bundled - User name, paths, runtime hashes, and app data redacted Expected: After native apps appear in Computer Use inventory, the session should support: - cua.getApp({ windowId }) - cua.computer.launch_app(...) - trusted @oai/sky access - targeted screenshots - accessibility/geometry aligned to the selected window - mouse and keyboard bound to the selected window Actual: Native inventory may work, but the target/window-control layer is unavailable. Full errors: Trusted RPC service is not configured: sky node_repl kernel unhandled rejection: Trusted RPC service is not configured: sky; kernel reset. Catch or handle async errors (including Promise rejections and EventEmitter 'error' events) to avoid kernel termination. cua.getApp is not a function Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'launch_app') Observed configuration regression: The generated unified Computer Use manifest can revert to browser-only settings: "NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES": "{\"browser\":\"@oai/browser-desktop/service\"}", "CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES": "browser" Expected settings: "NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES": "{\"browser\":\"@oai/browser-desktop/service\",\"sky\":\"@oai/sky/service\"}", "CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES": "browser,computer" Reproduction: 1. Observe: Trusted RPC service is not configured: sky Impact: - Cannot safely test Notepad mouse/keyboard input. - Cannot capture the correct selected app window. - Cannot validate coordinate geometry. - Cannot reliably target Chrome or Electron desktop applications. - The issue is external to the tested application; no application business logic is involved. Requested fix: 1. Always register Sky as a trusted RPC service when Windows Computer Use is enabled. 2. Ensure browser and computer surfaces are both enabled when native Computer Use is available. 3. Ensure the runtime API matches the documented API, including cua.getApp and cua.computer.launch_app. 4. Preserve or correctly regenerate native configuration after ChatGPT/Codex/plugin/runtime updates. 5. Ensure screenshots, accessibility tree, coordinates, mouse, and keyboard all target the same selected native window. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? Feedback ID: 01a0df3b-7ae9-7163-89d9-5c18b28dbac5 ### What is the expected behavior? The built-in Computer tool should initialize in the supported session and allow ChatGPT to inspect and interact with the Windows desktop and visible Chrome tabs after the user explicitly requests it. It should not require any third-party remote desktop tool. The built-in Computer tool is unavailable to the active conversation. The model recognizes the request but has no Computer tool exposed in its available tools. The task is redirected to Work mode or the model reports that it cannot directly interact with the desktop. The failure happens before any website or desktop interaction takes place, so this appears to be a tool/session initialization or tool-availability issue. ### Additional information Impact / repeated regression This issue has now been disrupting my work for approximately 5 days, beginning around September 25, 2026, and continuing through September 29, 2026. I am the CEO of a small nonprofit organization and I am building a volunteer coordination system called Beacon. The built-in Computer Use capability is important because the application needs to be validated against our already-open Better Impact and Gmail sessions without making live changes. This has become a recurring problem rather than a single failure. Timeline: September 25, 2026 - Built-in @Computer was reported as unavailable in the active session. - I repeatedly tried to continue Beacon Desktop testing using only the built-in Computer tool. - The system could understand the @Computer reference, but the actual Computer capability was not exposed to the chat. - Because of this, Beacon Desktop could not be opened or tested against the live browser workflow. - Work had to be stopped, moved between chats, or continued through GitHub/cloud-only tasks instead of completing the intended desktop validation. September 26, 2026 - We tested @Computer again in a new Work chat. - The tool was still not reliably exposed. - One attempt produced an unrelated control/session error before Beacon validation could even begin: "Automatic approval review failed: control returned an invalid credential refresh response." - This occurred before the Beacon application itself was tested, so it did not appear to be an application bug. September 28, 2026 - Significant additional time and model resources were spent trying to diagnose and recover Computer Use. - One audit consumed approximately 40% of the available usage allocation. - Later that day, the usage screen showed only about 4% of the 5-hour allowance remaining. - At another point, approximately 36% of the weekly allowance remained. - Computer Use also produced a "failed to write kernel assets" type error during investigation. - After further troubleshooting, two consecutive native inventory initializations later completed without reproducing the kernel-asset error. - This made the feature appear fixed again. September 29, 2026 - The issue has continued to recur. - After spending substantial resources getting Computer Use working, it can become unavailable again in another chat/session. - The same project is still not fully completed because the final live, read-only desktop/browser validation keeps being interrupted by Computer Use availability rather than by Beacon itself. Pattern observed: 1. Computer Use is unavailable. 2. Significant time and model usage are spent diagnosing or forcing the environment to initialize correctly. 3. It eventually appears to work. 4. Work resumes. 5. In a later session/chat, Computer Use is unavailable again. 6. More time and usage are spent repeating the same recovery process. This creates a repeated regression cycle. Resource / token impact: I cannot provide an exact token count because ChatGPT does not expose an exact per-session token-consumption total to me. However, I can document the visible usage impact: - One September 28 troubleshooting/audit session consumed approximately 40% of the available usage allocation. - Later the same day, only approximately 4% of the 5-hour allowance remained. - Weekly allowance was also materially reduced. - Multiple sessions over several days have been consumed repeating Computer Use diagnosis rather than completing the actual Beacon work. This is especially costly because the troubleshooting is not advancing the application itself. The resources are being consumed trying to restore access to a built-in tool that had already worked previously. Business impact: I run a nonprofit organization and do not have the time or technical resources to repeatedly troubleshoot the same ChatGPT platform capability. The Beacon Volunteer Coordinator project is intended to reduce administrative workload for a volunteer-driven charity. Instead, this recurring Computer Use issue has: - delayed completion of the Beacon Desktop project for multiple days; - required repeated Work chats and handoffs; - consumed a substantial portion of paid model usage; - forced me to repeat testing and troubleshooting; - interrupted continuity between project sessions; - prevented final live validation against Better Impact and Gmail; - caused work that was otherwise passing its automated tests to remain unfinished. This is particularly frustrating because the Beacon application itself has reached a fairly advanced validation state. At one point the current build had: - 76 Python tests passing - 128 TypeScript tests passing - TypeScript build passing - packaged executable dry-run passing - shared-BCC Gmail reconciliation bug fixed The remaining work required live, read-only Computer Use validation against the desktop application, Better Impact, and Gmail. Therefore the current blocker is not primarily the Beacon application. The recurring blocker is the unreliable availability of the built-in Computer tool between sessions. Expected reliability: Once built-in Computer Use is available for an eligible Windows/Work session, it should remain consistently available across continued work on that project, or provide a clear and actionable error explaining why it cannot initialize. It should not require repeated large troubleshooting sessions or "force" fixes simply to restore a capability that worked shortly beforehand. If a particular Work session cannot support Computer Use, the UI should make that clear before substantial work begins and ideally allow the user to start the correct Computer-enabled session without losing project context. Overall impact: Approximately five days of work have now been affected between September 25 and September 29, 2026. I cannot claim that every hour of those five days was lost exclusively to this bug, but it has repeatedly interrupted and slowed the same project across that period and has consumed a significant amount of my available model usage. For a nonprofit organization with limited time and resources, this level of repeated troubleshooting is a serious productivity issue.
